_comment: The instrument of ADR-0046, committed. Until 2026-08-18 the mutation pass existed only as a
number in that ADR (Stryker 9.6.1, 2973 mutants, 60.78%, 2h35 on 2026-08-05) and as a command
someone had typed once. A ratchet you cannot re-run is not a ratchet.
It mutates dist/ rather than src/ because the tests import dist/ — the same build the package
ships, so a killed mutant is a mutant killed in what users actually run.
COST, MEASURED 2026-08-20 ON AN IDLE MACHINE, AND THE QUALIFIER IS THE POINT: 4250 mutants over
the eleven modules, 960 of them in evidence.js alone, against a unit suite of 20 s.
Every earlier figure in this file was wrong, and wrong for one reason worth writing down. The
harness used spawnSync's timeout, which signals the direct child only; `node --test` isolates
each test file in its own process, so every timed-out run left about a dozen grandchildren alive,
still executing their mutant. They accumulated. Measured load average 78 on 8 cores, 32 orphans
still running after the driver had been killed, and at one point two copies of the verifier racing
each other. The suite was recorded as 105 s, then 84 s, then 38 s; idle and alone it is 20 s.
That contamination corrupts a mutation run in BOTH directions, which is what makes it worse than
mere slowness: a starved survivor is filed as a Timeout and vanishes into the detected column,
while a genuine hang was measured as an ordinary survivor. Neither error announces itself.
scripts/bounded-run.mjs is the fix — a detached process group killed whole on the deadline, plus
a lock so a second verifier cannot start. An instrument that a second copy of itself can falsify
was never measuring anything.
WHAT MAKES IT AFFORDABLE OVER TIME — four levers, and one that does NOT work here:
1. EARLY EXIT, ORDERED BY MEASURED COST (scripts/mutation-testcmd.sh). The suite's cost is very
unevenly spread: measured 2026-08-21 on an idle machine, 13 of 72 files are 68 s of the 86 s,
while the other 59 together are 17.6 s. The command runs the cheap files first and stops at
the first failure, so a KILLED mutant — the large majority — pays only for the cheap half,
while a SURVIVOR still pays for the whole suite, which is correct: proving that nothing kills
a mutant means running everything. Order cannot change a verdict, since a mutant is killed iff
some test fails; it only changes when we learn it. The split lives in test/unit-cost.json;
re-run `node scripts/test-cost.mjs` after the suite's shape changes. A stale file costs time
and never truth.
2. INCREMENTAL (on). Stryker keeps reports/mutation/incremental.json and re-tests only the
mutants a change can reach. The first pass is the expensive one; every later pass costs
roughly what the diff costs. This is the answer to 'and when the perimeter is bigger'.
3. CONCURRENCY 2, AND IT IS A CORRECTNESS SETTING RATHER THAN A SPEED ONE. Measured 2026-08-24:
the unit suite alone uses 310 % CPU — 3.1 cores — because `node --test` parallelises its own
files. So each Stryker worker costs ~3 cores, and the ceiling on an 8-core machine is TWO,
not four and certainly not seven.
This has now been got wrong twice, in the same direction, and the direction is what matters.
Seven workers (2026-08-19) produced load 78 and turned 199 survivors into 'detected'.
Dropping to four looked like the fix and was not: on 2026-08-24 the same 73-mutant range read
1 timeout on one run and 69 on the next, with load averaging 12 on 8 cores. Stryker counts a
Timeout as DETECTED, so oversubscription always errs toward flattery — a starved run reads as
a caught mutant.
The rule that replaces the guesswork: measure the suite's own CPU (`time node --test …`,
read the % figure) and set concurrency to floor(cores / that). Never pick it from the core
count alone, which is what treats the suite as single-threaded when it is not.
TIMEOUTS ARE VERIFIED, NOT TRUSTED. Stryker's threshold is timeoutMS + netTime * 1.5, and
no value of it is both tight enough to keep a hanging mutant cheap and loose enough to
guarantee a slow survivor is never starved — a mutant that loops forever and a mutant that
merely runs the whole suite are separated by contention, not by kind. So the threshold is
set for cost (120000, about 272 s) and scripts/mutation-timeouts.mjs re-runs every
Timeout-status mutant alone afterwards. Detected-by-timeout enters the register only when
it reproduces on an idle machine. Measuring the doubtful cases costs minutes; believing
them cost a false 100 % on 2026-08-19.
4. PER-MODULE, then PER-CHUNK runs (scripts/mutation-chunked.sh). Same total work, but a
pass that survives the laptop closing. Two passes were lost that way on 2026-08-18: the
second died on 'initial test run timed out' after 17 min of wall clock spent asleep, which
is why dryRunTimeoutMinutes is 30 against a measured 43 s baseline — a nap must cost a
retry, never a failed run. Chunks that are already on disk are never recomputed.
NOT a lever, measured 2026-08-18 rather than assumed: the tap runner with
coverageAnalysis 'perTest' — which is how Stryker normally runs only the tests covering a
mutant, and would have been worth 10-50x. `node --test` runs each test file in its own
process, so Stryker's per-test counters never come back: it reported 106 of 106 mutants as
'no coverage' on a module the suite genuinely exercises. That score would have been a
fiction, and a fast wrong number is worse than a slow right one. Revisit if Stryker gains a
node:test runner, or if the suite moves to a runner it can instrument.
RUN IT PER MODULE to get an affordable, resumable answer:
npx stryker run --mutate dist/lib/tool-adapters.js
The full net still judges each mutant (no test is excluded, so nothing is falsely reported as a
survivor); only the mutant count per run changes. The register is built module by module.
NEVER A GATE (decision 1): no threshold, `break` is null, and CI does not run this. A score in a
manifest would be a verdict nobody re-derived, which ADR-0045 forbids — runward does not do to
itself what it refuses from an operator.

rule: A module belongs in `mutate` when a mutant in it can change WHAT A CONSUMER ACTS ON: a
verdict, an exit code, or an emitted artifact someone re-derives. 'Imported by verdict.ts'
was the working criterion until 2026-08-24 and it is too narrow — sarif.js emits the verdict
as a machine contract a CI reads, and paths.js decides the byte-identity of a bundle across
operating systems. Neither is imported by the verdict core; a mutant in either is visible to
Every module under src/lib is in `mutate`, in `excluded`, or in `candidates`.
test/unit/mutation-perimeter.test.js fails when one is in none of them. That guard exists
because sarif.js shipped on 2026-08-17 emitting the verdict and was never added here:
the perimeter being DATA made it auditable, and nothing made it COMPLETE.

NARROWING FOR A ONE-OFF MEASUREMENT GOES ON THE COMMAND LINE, never in this file: `npx stryker run --mutate 'dist/lib/evidence.js:265-339' --force`. Editing `mutate` here redeclares the perimeter, so every other module becomes an orphan and test/unit/mutation-perimeter.test.js reddens — which it did on 2026-08-24 when this comment's author edited the file out of habit. The guard was right; the method was wrong.

excluded.styles: presentation only — colour and layout helpers; a mutant changes how a line looks and nothing a consumer acts on
excluded.constants: three constants and no branch; there is nothing here for a mutant to decide
excluded.regimes: the regime catalogue, data rather than logic; its contents are pinned by the OSCAL golden test
excluded.claims-rules: the forbidden-claim list, shipped as data via the runward/claims export; its semantics are pinned in both directions by test/unit/no-overclaim.test.js, which is the net a mutation pass would be re-deriving
excluded.write: a filesystem write helper with no decision of its own; its callers carry the branches
excluded.hooks: the operator's own escape hatch (ADR-0009) — runward runs what the operator wrote and judges none of it, so there is no verdict here to corrupt
excluded.harness: detects which coding-agent harness is present, to write its config; wrong detection is visible immediately at init and changes no verdict
excluded.rule-migrations: corpus migration bookkeeping, exercised end to end by test/audit-corpus.js on real corpora rather than by unit assertions
excluded.manifest-sync: keeps a scaffolded manifest in step with the corpus; it edits documents the operator then reviews, and the gate re-reads them from scratch
excluded.behavioral-proof: a readiness lens that is framed as a draft and never a compliance claim (see its own tests); it produces prose for a human, not a verdict

candidates.characterize: 855 lines behind `runward characterize`, the brownfield entry the README names as one of three user profiles, governed by five ADRs (0013, 0014, 0016, 0034, 0035). It emits `characterization.md`, so by the rule above it belongs in the perimeter: someone acts on those facts. Measured 2026-08-24 before deciding — the LIBRARY is at 89.5 % line and 77.5 % branch coverage across 19 tests, and ADR-0014's determinism moat is pinned byte-for-byte; the 20 % figure that looked alarming is the 80-line COMMAND wrapper, which carries nine decisions and no artifact. So this is a well-tested module of unknown mutation strength, not a blind spot. Held out on cost alone until `evidence` is closed, and it is the first candidate to admit after it — a document read as fact deserves to know whether its extraction is watched.
candidates.tools: 221 lines behind the committed-tool adapters. The adapters themselves (tool-adapters) are in the perimeter; this is the layer beneath them and it has never been measured separately.
candidates.ratify: The ADR-0066 ratification core: pure decision-application and the deterministic en-bloc sample, behind `runward ratify`. By the perimeter rule it belongs in `mutate` — a decision the operator signs rides on it. Held out until the consolidated post-0.37.1 re-measure pass that the 2026-09-02/03 wave of merged PRs already owes (several measured modules were touched); it enters `mutate` in that pass, with its survivors filed like every other module's.

_amendments: 2026-08-27 — `compliance` moved from candidates into `mutate`.
The note held it out with a condition ("Add when `evidence` is closed") and a reason: "one module
of eleven is instructed today, and widening first buys a bigger number and no more knowledge".
The CONDITION is not met — evidence still carries 144 filed holes. The REASON was falsified by
measurement, which is why the module moves anyway.
Three SHIPPED defects lived in compliance.js, every one found by adversarial audit and none by its
byte-for-byte golden test:
RWD-2026-0045 — the OSCAL pack was byte-identical between a green gate and a gate red on
eighteen unresolvable pointers, and recorded the verdict nowhere.
RWD-2026-0058 — it declared a control `implemented` when its only evidence was a sentence, and
the word 'prose' appeared zero times in the whole readiness document.
RWD-2026-0061 — it called a governance file 'present' in the same pass where `check` called it a
raw template.
Widening here would have bought knowledge three times over. The note's own text anticipated the
gap — "a real net but a single fixture" — and the audit proved that single fixture insufficient
three times. This is the perimeter RULE applied to new data, not an exception to it: a mutant in
this module changes an emitted artifact a regulated buyer consumes, which is the rule's own
criterion, and the module's original entry already said so ('it belongs in the perimeter on
principle').
Cost, so the trade is on the record: 468 lines against evidence.js's 1296, roughly a third, so an
expected few hundred mutants against evidence's 960. Measured on ubuntu-latest, never on a laptop
(ADR-0046 amendment 2026-08-26).
The held-out text, kept verbatim so the change is legible:

395 lines that assemble the OSCAL pack a regulated buyer consumes — an emitted artifact by the rule above, so it belongs in the perimeter on principle. Held out only until the register catches up: one module of eleven is instructed today, and widening first buys a bigger number and no more knowledge. Its byte-for-byte golden test is a real net but a single fixture. Add when `evidence` is closed.
